The mocked `Client` constructor args are not asserted for the new `types` option, and `datasourceTypeParser`/`RAW_TEXT_OIDS` (the actual behavioural core of this change — DATE/TIMESTAMP/TIMESTAMPTZ returned as raw text, everything else delegated to the default parser) has no unit test at all. It is only covered indirectly by the DATABASE_URL-gated e2e test, so if that lane is skipped the parser change ships with no coverage. A direct unit assertion (parser for TIMESTAMP returns input verbatim, parser for INT4 still parses to number) would be cheap.

coderabbit.summary: The `MONEY` assertion is locale-dependent and may fail on non-US clusters.
coderabbit.detail: **The `MONEY` assertion is locale-dependent and may fail on non-US clusters.** PostgreSQL formats the `money` type using the database's `lc_monetary` setting, which dictates the currency symbol and digit grouping. Since the test asserts the exact string `$1,234.56`, it will fail on databases configured with different locales. Either set `lc_monetary` to `en_US.UTF-8` in the test setup or avoid asserting the formatted string output.
